resolution: ReceptivePotencyTo (DEF-RECEPTIVE-POTENCY) is the potency of a recipient to an act it may already actually have, as De ente c.3 says of an intelligence's quiddity and its esse. InPotency (DEF-POTENCY) is being able to have a respect without actually having it. SUBSISTENT-INFINITY-FROM-RECEPTION uses only the first, and never the not-both law for InAct and InPotency, so an actually existing recipient is not contradicted by its receptive potency (see the 2026-10-31 reception note in docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md). Not forked (sense fork batch 3, #1233 B): the two senses have different Lean types. ReceptivePotencyTo relates a principle to the act it receives (Principle sort), while InPotency (DEF-POTENCY) is a predicate of a being in a respect, so no single use can be read in both and equivocation is already a type error. Within the being-in-a-respect reading, DISAMB-POTENCY's fork (POTENCY-SENSE-FORK-NO-SELF-MOTION) covers the potency senses of the prima via step.
